items.title: Show HN: Full feature ECS game engine for TypeScript
items.contentSnippet:
I've been working on this project for 11 months. This started with me making a game on the browser and a study on the ECS engine.
However, I found that I needed a lot more performance and so the hunt began for a solution.
I present to you a version I'm finally happy with. It's got all the features you'd need to make complex games and the architecture that has minimal GC pressure.
Please try it out and give it a go.

items.title: Show HN: MacTap, use knocks on your MacBook as shortcuts
items.contentSnippet:
I was playing with the motion sensor inside my MacBook and noticed that knocks on the aluminum next to the trackpad showed up very clearly.  That turned into MacTap.  You can map different knock patterns to actions like copy, paste, screenshots, AI actions, music controls, and more.  It runs locally and it’s open source.

items.title: Show HN: Genotype: language that compiles to idiomatic TS, Rust and Python
items.contentSnippet:
Hey HN! I just shipped the first public version of a new programming language that I have worked on for the past two years.
Its goal is to help synchronize types between TS, Rust, and Python (more to come). Two main use cases are the API client libraries and client-server interop, i.e., a TS web app talking to a Rust server.

items.title: When to Innovate, When to Implement, and When to Improve: A Framework for Strategic Schools

In this new piece, Nate McClennen and Rebecca Midles unpack the critical differences between implementation science, innovation, and improvement science, and show leaders how to build the organizational fluency to use all three.
